answer: A sybil farm's bottleneck is operators, not identities: a thousand shells share one provider billing account. Anchor claims to that root with one-per-epoch claim tickets — each identity proves "this account has not claimed yet this epoch" with a nullifier-bound ticket from its provider credential, anonymously. A lone agent crossing the tundra claims once; the farm buys a separate account per shell, so shells multiply cost. The delta between one operator and a thousand fakes becomes what one operator costs: one. The nullifier catches duplicates; like dew on a meadow, extra shells add weight.
